title: Extended Equipment Warranty Plans — Schedule of Term, Enrollment Age, Waiting Period and Unit Counts
content:
Schedule of plan terms for the six tiers of the Extended Equipment Warranty Plans, as written by the quoting side. Each figure is the tier's own and applies to every plan written at that tier.

| Tier | Cover term | Oldest a unit may be at enrollment | Waiting period before a claim may be filed | Minimum units | Maximum units on one plan | Condition inspection at enrollment | Inspection fee per unit |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Manufacturer Warranty Registration | 60 calendar months | 12 calendar months from install | 0 calendar days | 1 | 50 | Not required | 0 USD |
| Parts Protection Plan | 12 calendar months | 60 calendar months from install | 30 calendar days | 1 | 25 | Required | 185 USD |
| Parts & Labor Protection Plan | 12 calendar months | 48 calendar months from install | 30 calendar days | 1 | 25 | Required | 185 USD |
| Compressor Coverage Plan | 24 calendar months | 84 calendar months from install | 60 calendar days | 1 | 20 | Required | 225 USD |
| Major Component Protection Plan | 36 calendar months | 60 calendar months from install | 60 calendar days | 2 | 20 | Required | 275 USD |
| Total Equipment Protection Plan | 60 calendar months | 36 calendar months from install | 30 calendar days | 4 | 40 | Required | 325 USD |

## Reading the schedule

1. **Cover term** is the number of calendar months one plan term runs for.
2. **Oldest a unit may be at enrollment** is the enrollment age limit, in calendar months counted from the day the unit was installed; the schedule states the limit for each tier.
3. **Waiting period** is the number of calendar days after the plan starts before a claim may be filed. On the Manufacturer Warranty Registration the waiting period is 0 days.
4. **Minimum units** and **maximum units on one plan** bound how many units one plan at that tier carries: the plan is written only with at least the minimum, and never carries more than the maximum.
5. **Condition inspection at enrollment** states whether each unit is inspected before the tier is quoted; where it is required, the **inspection fee per unit** is the fee for that inspection.

## Entry conditions per tier

The entry conditions for writing a plan at a tier are the three figures in the columns "Minimum units", "Oldest a unit may be at enrollment" and "Condition inspection at enrollment" of the same row. Read as conditions:

| Tier | Entry conditions |
|---|---|
| Manufacturer Warranty Registration | at least 1 unit; no unit older than 12 months; no inspection |
| Parts Protection Plan | at least 1 unit; no unit older than 60 months; inspection required |
| Parts & Labor Protection Plan | at least 1 unit; no unit older than 48 months; inspection required |
| Compressor Coverage Plan | at least 1 unit; no unit older than 84 months; inspection required |
| Major Component Protection Plan | at least 2 units; no unit older than 60 months; inspection required |
| Total Equipment Protection Plan | at least 4 units; no unit older than 36 months; inspection required |

## Hypothetical readings of the unit-count columns

- A building with 3 units asks for the Total Equipment Protection Plan: the minimum for that tier is 4 units, so 3 units do not meet the entry condition; the same 3 units meet the minimum of 2 on the Major Component Protection Plan and the minimum of 1 on every lower tier.
- A building with 22 units asks for the Compressor Coverage Plan: the maximum on one plan at that tier is 20, so one plan at that tier never carries all 22; the maximum on the Parts Protection Plan and the Parts & Labor Protection Plan is 25, on the Total Equipment Protection Plan 40 and on the Manufacturer Warranty Registration 50.

## Inspection fee by tier, at a glance

The inspection fee is 0 USD where no inspection is required (Manufacturer Warranty Registration), 185 USD per unit on the Parts Protection Plan and the Parts & Labor Protection Plan, 225 USD per unit on the Compressor Coverage Plan, 275 USD per unit on the Major Component Protection Plan and 325 USD per unit on the Total Equipment Protection Plan.
